matID mask compared LINEAR palette values against sRGB-encoded pixels and silently dropped 8 of 10 materials
glass-gate vertex test used a 1 nm tolerance against float32 data whose ULP at this scale is 238 nm, and returned a wrong 'point sets differ'

set_paint wrote default_value on a LINKED Base Color, which does nothing - it produced two byte-identical renders and a confident wrong 'the paint does not respond'

CORRECTION_issued_in_session.retracted: rear2_v4.glb's carpaint and Rim_Alloy are '[1,1,1,1] metallic 1 rough 1 = the glTF-defaults flat-shell signature'
CORRECTION_issued_in_session.why_wrong: both materials carry baseColorTexture AND metallicRoughnessTexture (the file holds 4 images / 4 textures; the other six gate files hold zero). On a TEXTURED material those factors are the neutral MULTIPLIER and are correct. This is the exact trap CLAUDE.md records for the tyre probe, reproduced by me.
CORRECTION_issued_in_session.how_it_surfaced: the respray control on rear2_v4 returned mean delta EXACTLY 0.00 over 64,486 px with base and alt mean colour identical to the integer. An exact zero over 64k px is not physics, so I checked rather than published: the two PNGs were pixel-identical.
CORRECTION_issued_in_session.second_bug_in_my_own_rig: bl_render.set_paint wrote default_value onto a Base Color input that is LINKED to an Image Texture node, which does nothing. It would have reported 'paint does not respond' on ANY textured car.
fixes: set_paint detects a linked input, inserts a MULTIPLY MixRGB, and prints SET_PAINT/SET_PAINT_WARNING
paint_check requires not hasTexture before calling a material flat

re_run_result.retracted: 'the rear paint does not respond at all' - it does respond
re_run_result.NOT_a_ratio: the two are not apples-to-apples: untextured was a direct colour set, textured could only be a MULTIPLY tint over a baked texture, which yields neutral grey rather than blue. That is my METHOD, not a verdict on the file.
re_run_result.OPEN_not_asserted: a name-targeted respray rewrites baseColorFactor, which on a textured material also only multiplies the baked texture - so a baked-colour paint may not be resprayable to an arbitrary colour by factor rewrite. NOT TESTED. Cheap test: rewrite carpaint.baseColorFactor in the glTF and re-render, before the rear lineage's textures are carried into a merged car.
